title: Holy Grail
teaches: The Holy Grail as we trade it: a leader in a strong, young trend whose ADX pushed up and rose before the pullback makes its first touch of the rising 20-day EMA with the low holding over the 50-day, the buy is a market order as it trades over the prior day's high, the stop sits a few cents under the swing low the pullback just made, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest trailed on the 10-day, and a failed Grail closes that stock until it makes a new momentum high.

facts.quote: 1. The 14-period ADX must initially be greater than 30 and rising.
facts.claim: Raschke's rule 1: the 14-period ADX over 30 and rising at first, before the pullback.

facts.quote: 2. Look for a retracement in price to the 20 period exponential moving average. This will usually be accompanied by a turndown in the ADX.
facts.claim: Raschke's rule 2: a retracement to the 20-period exponential average, usually with the ADX turning down.

facts.quote: 3. When the price touches the 20 period moving average, put a buy stop above the high of the previous bar.
facts.claim: Raschke's rule 3: once price touches the average, a buy stop above the previous bar's high.

facts.quote: 4. Once filled, enter a protective sell stop at the newly formed swing low. Trail stops as profits grow.
facts.claim: Raschke's rule 4: the stop at the newly formed swing low; trail as profits grow.

facts.quote: Buy rules (sells are reversed)
facts.claim: Raschke: the buy rules are stated; sells are the reverse, so direction comes from the trend.

facts.quote: Therefore, any pullback from a new momentum high can be bought.
facts.claim: Raschke: a pullback from a new momentum high can be bought.

facts.quote: the majority of them have had Holy Grail patterns.
facts.claim: Raschke: most stocks that took part in the market's advance had Holy Grail patterns.

facts.quote: The 20 period exponential moving average often acts as support for stocks.
facts.claim: Raschke: the 20-period exponential average often acts as support.

facts.quote: This is a case where there is no reason to be in this trade.
facts.claim: Raschke's ETN lesson: a trade that does nothing is a trade with no reason to be in.

facts.quote: When you research this pattern, you should also look at cases when it fails.
facts.claim: Raschke: study the cases where the pattern fails.

facts.quote: The stock had a huge thrust up and pulled back nicely to the 20 period moving average. The ADX indicator was quite high.
facts.claim: Raschke's ETN example: a huge thrust, a nice pullback, a high ADX, and still no follow-through.

facts.quote: First, if a grail buy trade fails, I know I'm not going to look to buy pullbacks in that market.
facts.claim: Raschke: after a failed Grail she stops buying pullbacks in that market.

facts.quote: one that fails to hold the moving average.
facts.claim: Raschke defines a failed Grail as one that fails to hold the moving average.

facts.quote: in a trending market -- for Pete's sake, use market orders.
facts.claim: Raschke: in a trending market, use market orders.

facts.quote: I personally use a 20-period exponential moving average on all my markets.
facts.claim: Raschke uses a 20-period exponential moving average.

facts.quote: wait for the market to tip its hand and have that short-term momentum indicate what the market's going to do, and then wait for the first two- to three-day retracement to enter the market.
facts.claim: Raschke: momentum first, then the first two- to three-day retracement is the entry.

facts.quote: I avoid the markets where the ADX falls below 20 and is declining, because there's just not enough movement between the swings for me.
facts.claim: Raschke avoids markets where the ADX is under 20 and falling.

facts.quote: I use market orders most of the time.
facts.claim: Raschke uses market orders most of the time.

facts.quote: identify the up-trending stocks with the best relative strength at the beginning of a quarter.
facts.claim: Raschke picks up-trending stocks with the best relative strength.

facts.quote: In other words, I want to see only shallow retracements.
facts.claim: Raschke wants only shallow retracements.

facts.quote: I'm always looking at the swing highs or the swing lows.
facts.claim: Raschke reads stops and levels off the swing highs and swing lows.

facts.quote: The best setups will have confirming factors like the 3-10 oscillator making new momentum highs.
facts.claim: Raschke: the best setups have the 3-10 oscillator making new momentum highs.

facts.quote: By then you should be looking for a top.
facts.claim: Raschke: by the time the pullback shows up on the slowest time frames, look for a top.

facts.quote: 14-period ADX is initially above 30 and rising
facts.claim: Woods restates the filter: the 14-period ADX initially above 30 and rising.

facts.quote: Prices retrace down to 20-period simple moving average (SMA)
facts.claim: Woods describes the line as a 20-period simple average, not Raschke's exponential one.

facts.quote: First, a high ADX can mean that the trend is overdone and may reverse soon.
facts.claim: Woods' caution: a high ADX can mean the trend is overdone.

facts.quote: Second, gradual and protracted trends may unfold entirely without the ADX ever crossing above 30.
facts.claim: Woods' second caution: a slow, smooth trend may never push the ADX over 30.

facts.quote: Wilder suggests that a strong trend is present when ADX is above 25 and no trend is present when ADX is below 20.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: Wilder's strong-trend level is 25; under 20 there is no trend.

facts.quote: it can take around 150 periods of data to get true ADX values.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: a true ADX value needs around 150 periods of history.

facts.quote: Stop first (by default a few cents under the day's low or the prior day's low, F62); the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
facts.claim: A3: stop first; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.quote: The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule (B20).
facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up, never wider; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.quote: Shares = account × risk % ÷ (entry − stop), rounded down, then capped: the size is the SMALLER of the risk-based size and the position cap
facts.claim: A5: shares are account times risk percent, divided by entry minus stop, rounded down, then capped.

facts.quote: The full size at one price with one stop; no adding.
facts.claim: A5: the full size at one price with one stop; no adding.

facts.quote: "I almost never take a loss greater than 3%": the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy (a loss on the position, not the account).
facts.claim: A13: the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy.

facts.quote: Move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally. The first trim: the hard rule is a third at 3R; ideally anywhere from 3R to 6R, and in practice he mostly waits for 5R.
facts.claim: B19: breakeven between 2R and 5R; the hard rule for the first trim is a third at 3R.

facts.quote: A gap against the stop: the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. The low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.
facts.claim: B20: on a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

facts.quote: With a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
facts.claim: B20's ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.

facts.quote: No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report; hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R.
facts.claim: B22: no new buys in the 3 days before a report; hold through one only if up 5R.

facts.quote: Trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
facts.claim: B23: only stocks at $10 or more trading at least $20 million a day.

facts.quote: The 200-day line: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long; shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short.
facts.claim: B26: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, except a parabolic long.

facts.quote: No chasing: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.
facts.claim: C28: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

facts.quote: Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink (A5).
facts.claim: C28: chasing costs size, because the stop stays put and the distance grows.

facts.quote: Too stretched to buy: skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average.
facts.claim: C29: skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day average.

facts.quote: Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups, except parabolic and mean-reversion trades.
facts.claim: C31: buy leaders, an RS rating of 80 or more in a strong group.

facts.quote: A climax run on your own long (Bracco's parabolic burst): sell a big part into it, a judgment call.
facts.claim: C34: sell a big part into a climax run.

facts.quote: Setup grades set the size: A and B setups at normal size; A+ sized up; B- or lower sized down.
facts.claim: D38: A and B at normal size; A+ sized up; B- or lower sized down.

facts.quote: Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head.
facts.claim: D41: a real stop order with the broker.

facts.quote: Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume; illiquid stocks are not even watched.
facts.claim: D42: never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.

facts.quote: After the first third at 3R: another third at 5R, then trail the last third; adjustable.
facts.claim: E51: another third at 5R, then trail the last third.

facts.quote: Default trail: the 10-day average for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.
facts.claim: E52: trail the 10-day for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.

facts.quote: Entries are market orders.
facts.claim: E57: entries are market orders.

facts.quote: No new buys outside regular trading hours.
facts.claim: E58: no new buys outside regular hours.

facts.quote: The stop sits a few cents under the day's low, not exactly on it.
facts.claim: F62: the stop sits a few cents under the low, not exactly on it.

facts.quote: If a stock opens above a trim level (3R, 5R), take that trim at the open.
facts.claim: F63: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.

facts.quote: The market reading as a guide (A10): Green, full risk per grade and up to 10 positions; Yellow, smaller and fewer; Orange, only A+ setups; Red, mostly cash and shorts.
facts.claim: F65: Green full risk; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange only A+; Red mostly cash and shorts.

facts.quote: After a market correction, when the reading turns Green again, start with a few positions and add more only as the first ones work
facts.claim: F68: after a correction, start with a few positions and add as they work.

facts.quote: After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule.
facts.claim: B21: after a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade.

facts.quote: The same stock: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month.
facts.claim: E56: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month on one stock.

facts.quote: computed on at least 150 sessions of history. Not the scanner's home-made average.
facts.claim: The ADX is the textbook Wilder ADX on at least 150 sessions of history, not a home-made average.

facts.quote: The scanner's plain-sum ADX read 29.9 on a chop chart where the Wilder ADX read 17.7
facts.claim: A home-made ADX read 29.9 on a chop chart where the true Wilder ADX read 17.7.

facts.quote: Direction comes from price, not the ADX: on the ADX session the close was above the 20 EMA, and the EMA is higher than 10 sessions earlier. +DI over -DI is not a gate.
facts.claim: Direction comes from price: the close above a rising 20 EMA on the ADX session; +DI over -DI is not a gate.

facts.quote: A new momentum high first: the highest close of the last 20 sessions was made within the 10 sessions before the touch.
facts.claim: The momentum-high test: the highest close of the last 20 sessions, made within the 10 sessions before the touch.

facts.quote: Close above the 200-day SMA.
facts.claim: Location: the close above the 200-day SMA.

facts.quote: Not right after a climax run: check Bracco's parabolic signs before buying. A very high ADX after a near-vertical climb can mean the trend is overdone.
facts.claim: Not right after a climax run: check Bracco's parabolic signs; a very high ADX after a vertical climb can mean overdone.

facts.quote: The line is the 20-day exponential moving average of closes. Not a 20 SMA, not the 21 EMA.
facts.claim: The line is the 20-day EMA of closes, not a 20 SMA, not the 21 EMA.

facts.quote: Length: 2 to 10 sessions from the momentum high to the touch.
facts.claim: Length: 2 to 10 sessions from the momentum high to the touch.

facts.quote: A shallow, orderly pullback of 2 to 5 sessions is the A+ version; 6 to 10 sessions is an A or B.
facts.claim: A shallow, orderly 2 to 5 session pullback is the A+; 6 to 10 sessions is an A or B.

facts.quote: No depth rule beyond the line itself. The touch session's low holds above the 50-day SMA; if it does not, it is a 50-day pullback (setup 12), not a Holy Grail.
facts.claim: No depth rule beyond the line; the touch low holds above the 50-day, or it is a 50-day pullback.

facts.quote: Volume is not a gate. No source requires it. Lighter volume on the pullback is a grade plus.
facts.claim: Volume is not a gate; lighter volume on the pullback is a grade plus.

facts.quote: A+ cue: the touch session shows buyers, closing in its upper half
facts.claim: The A+ cue: the touch session shows buyers, closing in its upper half.

facts.quote: Before the trigger, the setup is void after a close below the 50-day SMA, or after 5 sessions from the first touch with no trigger.
facts.claim: The setup is void after a close under the 50-day, or after 5 sessions from the first touch with no trigger.

facts.quote: A few cents under the newly formed swing low: the lowest low from the touch session through the trigger session.
facts.claim: The stop: a few cents under the swing low, the lowest low from the touch session through the trigger session.

facts.quote: Not the pullback low minus 1 ATR (the scanner's stop). That puts the risk past 4% before the bar's own range is added.
facts.claim: Not the pullback low minus 1 ATR: that puts the risk past 4% before the bar's own range is added.

facts.quote: if the long stops out, or price closes back under the EMA and then under the touch low, no more pullback buys in that stock until it makes a new momentum high
facts.claim: A failed Grail: no more pullback buys in that stock until it makes a new momentum high.

facts.quote: A re-buy is only a fresh trigger with its own stop.
facts.claim: A re-buy is only a fresh trigger with its own stop.

facts.quote: Check the ADX. Both are a pullback to a rising 20 EMA bought on the turn
facts.claim: The 20 EMA pullback tell: check the ADX; both setups are a pullback to a rising 20 EMA.

facts.quote: No ADX push, it is the plain 20 EMA pullback.
facts.claim: Without an ADX push before the pullback, it is the plain 20 EMA pullback (setup 11).

facts.quote: Trail the last third: sell on a close below the 10-day average.
facts.claim: This setup's trail: the last third sold on a close below the 10-day average.

facts.quote: The 10-day, not the 21-day: a stock that has just pushed its ADX
facts.claim: The 10-day rather than the 21-day, because a stock that just pushed its ADX is usually moving fast.

facts.quote: Count the closes under the line. A Holy Grail touch holds the 20 EMA and its low stays above the 50-day; a Remount has lost its 50-day or 200-day for 5 or more straight closes and is buying it back.
facts.claim: The Remount tell: a Grail touch holds the 20 EMA above the 50-day; a Remount lost its 50 or 200-day for 5 or more closes.

facts.quote: A Slingshot's closes slip under the 4-day EMA of the highs for 3 to 7 sessions and the buy is the close back over it; a Holy Grail touches the 20-day EMA and buys over the prior day's high.
facts.claim: The Slingshot tell: closes under the 4-day EMA of the highs, bought on the close back over it; a Grail touches the 20-day EMA.

facts.quote: An Oops opens under the prior close, trades under the prior day's low and reclaims the prior close the same day; the Grail's trigger is over the prior day's high, after a touch of the 20 EMA.
facts.claim: The Oops tell: opens under the prior close, trades under the prior low, reclaims the prior close the same day.

facts.quote: A U&R dips under a prior low and closes back above it within 3 sessions; a Holy Grail undercuts no low, it touches a rising average and clears the prior day's high.
facts.claim: The U&R tell: a dip under a prior low reclaimed within 3 sessions; a Grail undercuts no low.

facts.quote: RS rating 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
facts.claim: Leadership: RS 80 or more in one of the strongest groups.

facts.quote: hg.leadership: RS 90 or more, top group
facts.claim: The A+ row: RS 90 or more, top group.

facts.quote: hg.leadership: lagging its group
facts.claim: The B- row: lagging its group.

facts.quote: Green market: full risk. Yellow: smaller and fewer. Orange: A+ only. Red: mostly cash and shorts below the 200-day.
facts.claim: Green full risk; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange A+ only; Red mostly cash and shorts.

facts.quote: Reading the ADX as direction. It measures strength; a strong downtrend also has a high ADX.
facts.claim: A named mistake: reading the ADX as direction; it measures strength.

facts.quote: Treating the ADX turning down in the pullback as a sell. Raschke expects it.
facts.claim: A named mistake: treating the ADX turning down in the pullback as a sell.

facts.claim: A named mistake: buying the touch instead of the trigger.

facts.quote: Using a 20 SMA because a web page said so. Raschke names the exponential average every time.
facts.claim: A named mistake: using a 20 SMA; Raschke names the exponential average every time.

facts.quote: Setting the stop a full ATR under the low. The house stop is a few cents under the swing low.
facts.claim: A named mistake: a stop a full ATR under the low.

facts.quote: Chasing a gap over the trigger by more than 4%.
facts.claim: A named mistake: chasing a gap over the trigger by more than 4%.

facts.quote: Buying a Holy Grail right after a climax run. A very high ADX can mean overdone; check Bracco's parabolic signs.
facts.claim: A named mistake: buying a Holy Grail right after a climax run.

facts.quote: Never raise the stop to make it fit.
facts.claim: Never raise the stop to make it fit the size.

facts.quote: A real stop order with the broker. It only moves up.
facts.claim: A real stop order with the broker; it only moves up.

facts.quote: hg.length: a deep or sloppy pullback with big red days
facts.claim: The B- row: a deep or sloppy pullback with big red days.

facts.quote: hg.touch_buyers: the touch session closes in its upper half, or shows the intraday turn

facts.claim: The B- row: right after a climax run, several of Bracco's parabolic boxes ticked.

walkthroughs.title: CI, October 2000: the textbook first touch
steps: CI, October 2000. A strong thrust off the 50-day, then seven quiet red days into the rising 20-day EMA.
Context checks out: above the 200-day, the first touch since the push, the low holding over the 50-day.
2000-10-26: it trades over the prior day's high. Buy at market, 36.72. Stop a few cents under the swing low, 36.03.
Failure mode: the pullback keeps falling and never clears the high. Instead it reaches 3R in 2 sessions. Trim a third.

walkthroughs.title: EXPD, March 2006: the two- to three-day retracement
steps: EXPD, March 2006. A leader makes a new momentum high, then rests three days, 3.6% deep, to the 20-day EMA.
Raschke's first two- to three-day retracement in one picture. The touch holds above the 50-day; volume is not a gate.
2006-03-09: it clears the prior day's high. Buy at market, 38.93. Stop a few cents under the swing low, 38.14.
Failure mode: a late, slow trigger after a long run. Instead, 3R in three sessions: a third off, stop to breakeven.

walkthroughs.title: LITE, July 2025: touch and trigger the same day
steps: LITE, July 2025. The cycle's leader pulls back seven days, 6.4% deep, into the rising 20-day EMA.
Touch and trigger on the same day: the range reaches the line, then price clears the prior day's high.
Buy at market, 91.78. Stop under the swing low, 88.88. 3R in five sessions: a third off, breakeven.
Then the parabolic leg Bracco warns about. A third at 5R; sell a big part into a climax run; trail the rest.

questions.q: Which line does the Holy Grail pull back to?
questions.why: The 20-day EMA of closes. Raschke names the exponential average every time. A 20 SMA is a web page's rewrite; the 21 EMA belongs to other scans.
questions.lesson_line: Twenty-day, exponential, closes. Draw the right line before you judge the touch.

wrong.The 20-day simple average: Some web pages say simple. Raschke says exponential, and so does our card.
wrong.The 21-day EMA: The 21 is the line on our other pullback scans, not this one.
wrong.The 50-day average: The 50-day is the floor under the touch, not the line it touches.

questions.q: The ADX tells you the trend's direction as well as its strength.
questions.why: False. The ADX measures strength; a strong downtrend also has a high ADX. Direction comes from price: the close above a rising 20 EMA.
questions.lesson_line: The ADX says how hard the trend is pushing, not which way. Price says which way.

questions.q: Where does the stop go after a Holy Grail fill?
choices: A few cents under the swing low
A full ATR under the pullback low
At the 20-day EMA, where it touched
questions.answer: A few cents under the swing low
questions.why: A few cents under the newly formed swing low: the lowest low from the touch session through the trigger session. Raschke's rule 4 says the same.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the low the pullback just made.

wrong.A full ATR under the pullback low: That is a scanner's stop, not ours. It puts the risk past 4% before the bar's own range.
wrong.At the 20-day EMA, where it touched: The line is where it touched, not where the trade is wrong. The swing low is.
wrong.At the 50-day moving average: Too far. A few cents under the swing low, usually within about 3%.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.why: 50. The touch session's low holds above the 50-day. If it does not, it is a 50-day pullback, a different setup.
questions.lesson_line: The touch holds the line, and the low holds the 50. Both, or it is not this.
questions.sentence: The touch session's low must hold above the ___-day average, or it is a different pullback.

questions.q: Light volume on a Holy Grail pullback is a grade plus, but heavy volume does not rule it out.
questions.why: True. Volume is not a gate; no source requires it. Lighter volume on the pullback is a grade plus, nothing more.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet volume into the line is a plus, not a must.

questions.q: The market reading is Orange. Which Holy Grails may you buy?
questions.why: Only A+ setups. Green is full risk; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange only A+; Red mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market before the line. Orange buys A+ and nothing else.

wrong.Any setup at full size: That is Green. Orange narrows you to A+.
wrong.None, Orange means cash: Red is mostly cash. Orange still allows the best setups.
wrong.Any setup at half size: Orange is about grade, not size. A B setup stays on the bench.

questions.q: We buy Holy Grails in leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in a strong group.
questions.why: True. Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups. Raschke picks the up-trending stocks with the best relative strength.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback in a laggard is a laggard pulling back. Buy the leaders.

questions.q: Our card's momentum-high test: the highest close of the last 20 sessions was made when?
choices: In the 10 sessions before the touch
On the touch session or just after
Within the 5 sessions before the touch
questions.answer: In the 10 sessions before the touch
questions.why: Within the 10 sessions before the touch. A new momentum high comes first; Raschke buys the pullback from a new momentum high.
questions.lesson_line: Fresh strength first, then the rest. A stale high is not momentum.

wrong.On the touch session or just after: The touch is the pullback. The high has to come before it.
wrong.Within the 5 sessions before the touch: The window is 10 sessions, not 5. A 5-session length is the A+ row, a different test.
wrong.Anywhere in the last 20 sessions: The 20 sessions only set which close is the highest. That high must sit inside the last 10.

questions.q: An ADX reading built on a few weeks of bars is as good as one built on a long history.
questions.why: False. It can take around 150 periods of data to get true ADX values. Our ADX is computed on at least 150 sessions, never a home-made average.
questions.lesson_line: A short-window ADX is a guess. Use the real Wilder ADX on a long history.

questions.q: What is it?
choices: A 50-day pullback, not a Holy Grail
A Holy Grail; it closed back above
questions.answer: A 50-day pullback, not a Holy Grail
questions.why: A 50-day pullback. The touch low must hold above the 50-day; this one went under it. It was stopped at 0R.
questions.lesson_line: Through the 20 and under the 50 is a different setup with its own rules.

wrong.A Holy Grail; it closed back above: The close does not fix the low. The low broke the 50-day, and that is the gate.
wrong.A Remount of the 50-day: A Remount needs 5 or more straight closes under the line first. This was one dip.

questions.story: The touch session dips through the 20 EMA. Its low prints 106.26, under the 50-day at 107.16. It closes back above the 50-day.

questions.q: At the trigger, one stock sits 7% above its 10-day average and another sits 13% above. Which do we skip?
questions.why: Only the one 13% above. A long more than 10% above its 10-day average is too stretched to buy, and 7% is inside that line. All ten of our examples filled within 2.5% of the 10-day.
questions.lesson_line: A stock at its line is rarely stretched. When it is, pass.

wrong.Both of the two stocks: 7% is under the 10% line, so that one still passes the stretch rule.
wrong.Only the one 7% above: Backwards. The further above the 10-day, the more stretched the entry.
wrong.Neither of the two stocks: 13% is past the 10% line, so that one is skipped.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.why: 4%. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the trigger and I am done. I would rather miss it than chase it.
questions.sentence: Never buy a Holy Grail trigger more than ___% above it, gap or no gap.

questions.q: The Holy Grail stop is a real stop order with the broker, not a level you watch in your head.
questions.why: True. Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head. It only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: A stop in your head is a debate. A stop with the broker is an appointment.

questions.q: By our card, how long is a Holy Grail pullback, momentum high to touch?
questions.why: 2 to 10 sessions from the momentum high to the touch. Raschke's first two- to three-day retracement sits inside it.
questions.lesson_line: Days, not weeks. A pullback that drags on has lost the thrust.

wrong.1 session at most: A one-day dip is too short to count. The card starts at 2.
wrong.10 to 20 sessions: Past 10 sessions the thrust has gone. That is a base, not a Grail.
wrong.Six weeks or more: Six weeks is a base. A Holy Grail is a rest of days.

questions.q: A Holy Grail touch under the 200-day is still a buy if the trend is strong enough.
questions.why: False. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. The close is above the 200-day, or it is no trade.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, there is no Holy Grail to buy.

questions.q: A steady climber touches its rising 20 EMA. No ADX push came before the dip. Which setup is it?
choices: A Holy Grail, ADX or no ADX
questions.why: The plain 20 EMA pullback. Both are a pullback to a rising 20 EMA bought on the turn. Only the Holy Grail needs an ADX push before the touch.
questions.lesson_line: Same picture, one difference: the ADX. Check it before you name it.

wrong.A Holy Grail, ADX or no ADX: The Grail is the 20 EMA pullback with an ADX push in front of it. No push, no Grail.
wrong.A Remount of the 50-day: A Remount has lost its 50 or 200-day for five or more closes. This stock touched a rising 20 EMA.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Sell at the stop; a planned loss
Hold; the line will catch it
questions.answer: Sell at the stop; a planned loss
questions.why: Sell at the stop. The stop is the exit; it only moves up, never wider. This one went on day 1 and the low 20 sessions later sat 7.9% under the buy.
questions.lesson_line: A loss taken at plan is the system working.

wrong.Hold; the line will catch it: The line already failed to hold. Holding and hoping is the named mistake.
wrong.Widen the stop under the 50-day: The stop only moves up, never wider.
wrong.Add; it is cheaper now: Full size at one price with one stop; no adding.

questions.story: You bought at 49.79 with the stop at 48.55 after a first touch of the 20 EMA. The next session trades through the stop.

questions.q: How much of the position do we sell at the first trim on a Holy Grail winner?
questions.why: A third, at 3R. That is the hard rule; the plan sells in thirds. The next third comes at 5R and the last third rides the trail.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, trail the rest.

wrong.Half, at 3R: Too much. The plan sells in thirds, so the first trim is a third.
wrong.A quarter, at 3R: The plan sells in thirds, not quarters.
wrong.All of it, at 3R: That sells the whole position. The last third rides the trail.

questions.q: Bought at 36.72 with the stop at 36.03. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 38.79. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. CI reached it in 2 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: A Holy Grail that triggers two sessions before an earnings report is still a buy.
questions.why: False. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. If it is still a setup after the report, it can trigger again.
questions.lesson_line: A trigger inside the earnings window is a coin flip with a story. Wait.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: Yes; the trigger just fired today
Yes, but at half the usual size
questions.why: No. Five sessions from the first touch with no trigger and the setup is void. This one reached 4.4R anyway; the rule is about staleness, not prediction.
questions.lesson_line: A trigger that takes a week to come is not the thrust you measured.

wrong.Yes; the trigger just fired today: It fired late. The setup went void after five sessions with no trigger.
wrong.Yes, but at half the usual size: Size does not fix a stale setup. The rule is no trade.

questions.story: The touch of the 20 EMA was six sessions ago. Price never cleared the prior day's high. Today it finally does.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.why: Momentum. After a failed Grail, no more pullback buys in that stock until it makes a new momentum high. Raschke: if a grail buy fails, she stops buying pullbacks in that market.
questions.lesson_line: A failed Grail closes the door on that stock until it proves strength again.
questions.sentence: After a failed Grail, no more pullback buys in that stock until it makes a new ___ high.

questions.q: A Holy Grail is bought at one price with one stop; adding on a second dip is not our way.
questions.why: True. The full size at one price with one stop; no adding.
questions.lesson_line: One price, one stop, full size. The second dip is a different decision.

questions.q: Fill 50.27, stop 48.75. How far below the fill is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 3.02%. The fill minus the stop, divided by the fill. About the 3% the stop usually sits within; AMBA's line held to the cent.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
choices: Get out, the gap is past 2R
questions.why: 69.40. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. That low is inside the 2R ceiling, so it is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Sell at the open, 69.90: The gap rule gives it the first 30 minutes. The 30-minute low is the decision, not the open.
wrong.No stop until it reclaims 70.50: There is always a stop. The new one is the 30-minute low.
wrong.Get out, the gap is past 2R: The 30-minute low is inside 2R here. The ceiling has not been hit.

questions.story: You bought at 72.00 with the stop at 70.50. It gaps open at 69.90, under your stop. The first 30-minute bar's low is 69.40.

questions.q: What do you check before you buy?
choices: The volume on the touch day
questions.why: Bracco's parabolic signs. A very high ADX after a near-vertical climb can mean the trend is overdone. Here the first touch was the start of April's correction.
questions.lesson_line: The first rest after a vertical run is often the top, not a rest.

wrong.Nothing; every box ticks: The boxes do not see a climax. Woods: a high ADX can mean the trend is overdone.
wrong.The volume on the touch day: Volume is a grade cue here, not the risk. The run itself is the risk.
wrong.The 50-day's slope: The 50-day is rising after a run like that. It cannot warn you.

questions.story: Every box ticks: a strong ADX push and a 5-day pullback to the 20 EMA. The stop is 87.57 against a 90.11 buy, 2.8%. The stock is in the third month of a near-vertical run.

questions.q: When does the stop move to breakeven on a Holy Grail winner?
choices: 2R to 5R, often at the first trim
The morning after the entry session
Never; the stop is the stop
questions.answer: 2R to 5R, often at the first trim
questions.why: Between 2R and 5R, ideally. The first trim at 3R is the natural moment.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven between 2R and 5R. Earlier is noise; later is giving it back.

wrong.The morning after the entry session: Too early. Breakeven waits until 2R at the earliest.
wrong.Never; the stop is the stop: The stop only moves up. Moving it up to breakeven is allowed.
wrong.As soon as it reaches 1R: Too soon. Breakeven waits until 2R at the earliest.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Sell a third at the open
Move the stop up and hold
questions.answer: Sell a third at the open
questions.why: Sell a third at the open. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open. The 3R third comes off right there.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through a trim level is the trim. Take it at the open.

wrong.Wait for the close: The level is already passed. Waiting gives the gap a chance to fill.
wrong.Sell everything: A third at 3R. The rest waits for 5R and the trail.
wrong.Move the stop up and hold: The stop moves up too, but the trim is the rule at the open.

questions.story: Your Holy Grail long sits at 2.5R at Thursday's close. Friday it gaps open to 3.4R.

questions.q: A shallow, orderly pullback of 2 to 5 sessions is the A+ version; 6 to 10 sessions grades A or B.
questions.why: True. A shallow, orderly pullback of 2 to 5 sessions is the A+ version; 6 to 10 sessions is an A or B. Raschke wants only shallow retracements.
questions.lesson_line: Short and shallow is the best Grail. Long and sloppy still trades, smaller.

questions.q: Buy this touch?
choices: No; wait for a new momentum high
Yes; the ADX is still high
Yes; it is the same setup
questions.answer: No; wait for a new momentum high
questions.why: No. After a failed Grail, no more pullback buys until a new momentum high. The 3R level did print 32 sessions later, but only after that new high.
questions.lesson_line: The stock has to earn the next pullback buy with new strength.

wrong.Yes; the ADX is still high: The ADX alone does not reopen it. Price has to make a new momentum high first.
wrong.Yes; it is the same setup: It is the same stock after a failed Grail. That is the named mistake.

questions.story: You bought at 113.96, stop 111.34. Stopped the next morning. Nine of the next ten closes sit under the 20 EMA. No new high since; now it dips to the line again.

questions.q: The last third of a Holy Grail winner trails which line, by our card?
questions.why: The 10-day, sold on a close below it. Our default trail is the 10-day for fast movers; a stock that just pushed its ADX is usually moving fast.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the 10-day. Sell the close below it, not the touch.

wrong.The 21-day; it is steadier: The 21-day is for steadier names. A fresh ADX push is a fast mover.
wrong.The 20 EMA, Raschke's line: The line is the entry's line. The trail is the 10-day.
wrong.The 50-day: Too far behind. The trail is the 10-day, sold on a close below it.

questions.q: Keep the alert or drop it?
choices: Keep it; a trend needs time
questions.why: Drop it. Five sessions from the first touch with no trigger and the setup is void. A stock that needs that long to clear a prior high has left the thrust.
questions.lesson_line: The trigger comes fast or it does not come. Five sessions and the alert goes.

wrong.Keep it; a trend needs time: A Holy Grail trigger comes within days. A week of waiting is the tell that it is stale.
wrong.Buy the close instead: Buying without a trigger is buying the touch. That is the named mistake.

questions.story: The touch was Monday. It is the next Tuesday, the sixth session, and price still has not cleared the prior day's high.

questions.q: Was that loss a mistake?
choices: No; a planned loss at the stop
Yes; the stop was too tight
Yes; never buy a slow pullback
questions.answer: No; a planned loss at the stop
questions.why: No. The stop is the exit, and the loss was 1R. The 3R level printed 18 sessions later without us; a re-buy needs its own fresh trigger.
questions.lesson_line: You will take this loss again. It is the cost of being there for the ones that work.

wrong.Yes; sell at +0.54R next time: The first trim is a third at 3R. Selling at half an R is fear, not a rule.
wrong.Yes; the stop was too tight: A few cents under the swing low is the rule, about 3% here. Nothing argues for wider.
wrong.Yes; never buy a slow pullback: The pullback was fine. The trade just did not work, and the stop kept it small.

questions.story: Bought at 56.66, stop 54.95. It reached +0.54R, then five sessions of drift. On day five the stop goes.

questions.q: Two Holy Grails, same picture. One has an RS rating of 92 in a top group; the other lags its group. Which grades A+?
choices: The laggard; it has room to run
Both; RS is not on the card
questions.why: The RS 92 leader. Our A+ row is RS 90 or more in a top group; lagging its group is the B- row. Raschke picks the best relative strength.
questions.lesson_line: Same shape, different stock. The leader gets the size.

wrong.The laggard; it has room to run: Room to run is a story. Lagging its group is the B- row.
wrong.Both; RS is not on the card: RS is on the card twice: the gate at 80 and the A+ cue at 90.

questions.q: A Holy Grail position may be up to 5% of the stock's average daily volume if the stop is tight.
questions.why: False. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume; a tight stop cannot catch an overnight gap.
questions.lesson_line: One percent of the daily volume, and not a share more.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 38.93, stop 38.14. How many shares?
questions.why: 316. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. That is about a quarter of the account, under the 40% cap. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Which touch is the A+ cue?
choices: The one closing in its upper half
The one closing on its low
Neither; the close does not matter
questions.answer: The one closing in its upper half
questions.why: The one closing in its upper half. The A+ cue is a touch session that shows buyers, closing in its upper half or showing the intraday turn.
questions.lesson_line: A touch that closes strong is buyers stepping in at the line. That is the picture.

wrong.The one closing on its low: A close on the low is sellers still in charge at the line.
wrong.Neither; the close does not matter: The close is the one thing the touch day tells you about the buyers.

questions.story: Two touches of the 20 EMA on the same kind of trend. One closes near the top of its range. The other closes on its low.

questions.q: The ADX turning down while the stock pulls back to the line kills the setup.
questions.why: False. Raschke expects the pullback to be accompanied by a turndown in the ADX. Treating that turndown as a sell is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: The ADX cools on every rest. That is the rest, not the end.

questions.q: Where is our stop?
questions.why: A few cents under 48.75, the swing low. A full ATR under the low puts the risk past 4% before the bar's own range is added.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is where the setup is wrong, not a volatility cushion under it.

wrong.46.75; give it some room: Room is a bigger loss, not a better trade. The named mistake is a stop a full ATR under the low.
wrong.At the 20 EMA line: The line is where it touched, not where the setup is wrong. The swing low is.

questions.story: The swing low is 48.75 and the ATR is 2.00. A scan suggests a stop at 46.75, a full ATR under the low.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Pass; Red is mostly cash and shorts
Buy it; A+ setups trade in any market
questions.answer: Pass; Red is mostly cash and shorts
questions.why: Pass. Red means mostly cash and shorts. Raschke found Grails in stocks riding the market's advance, and a Red market is not one.
questions.lesson_line: The best pullback in a Red market is a pullback. Sit on your hands.

wrong.Buy it; A+ setups trade in any market: Orange allows A+. Red is mostly cash and shorts.
wrong.Buy half size: Half size in a Red market is half a mistake.

questions.story: The reading is Red. A leader shows a clean first touch of its 20 EMA after a strong push and trades over the prior day's high.

questions.q: Buy again?
choices: Yes, as a fresh trade, own stop
No; one try per stock per month
Yes, with a wider stop this time
questions.answer: Yes, as a fresh trade, own stop
questions.why: Yes. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop. The new momentum high and fresh ADX push reopened the door.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a verdict on the setup. A fresh trigger after new strength is a new trade.

wrong.No; one try per stock per month: The limit is 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, not one.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop this time: The stop is the new swing low again. A wider stop to avoid a repeat is the mistake.

questions.story: Your Holy Grail stopped out last week. Since then the stock made a new momentum high, the ADX pushed up again, and it pulled back to the line. Today it trades over the prior day's high.

questions.q: A climax run in your Holy Grail position is the moment to sell a big part into it.
questions.why: True. A climax run on your own long, Bracco's parabolic burst: sell a big part into it, a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: Sell partials into strength. A vertical leg is strength to sell into.

questions.q: Buy or pass?
choices: Buy; the news gap confirms the move
Buy at half the normal size
Buy, with a much wider stop
questions.why: Pass. 60.00 is more than 4% over 56.50. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the swing low, so the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: A gap over the trigger is a gift you decline. Four percent and done.

wrong.Buy; the news gap confirms the move: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Buy at half the normal size: Half of a bad entry is still a bad entry.
wrong.Buy, with a much wider stop: A wider stop to fit a late entry is the mistake, not the fix.

questions.story: The trigger is the prior day's high at 56.50. News hits and the stock opens at 60.00, straight through it.

questions.q: The momentum-high close was 40.00 and the swing low is 37.60. How deep is the pullback, in percent?
questions.why: 6.0%. The high minus the low, divided by the high. Our card sets no depth rule beyond the line; the touch low holds the 50-day. AMBA's 7.8% was the deepest of our ten.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the dip, then look at the 50-day. Depth is a picture, not a gate.

questions.q: Before the trigger comes, the stock closes under its 50-day. The setup?
questions.why: Void. Before the trigger, a close below the 50-day SMA ends the setup.
questions.lesson_line: The 50-day is the floor. Lose it before the trigger and the Grail is gone.

wrong.Still live for 5 sessions: The 5 sessions are for a trigger that never comes. A close under the 50-day ends it at once.
wrong.A buy at the 50-day instead: That is a different setup with its own rules. It is not a Holy Grail.

questions.q: Which setup is it?
choices: A Remount, not a Holy Grail
A Holy Grail; the line was retaken
questions.answer: A Remount, not a Holy Grail
questions.why: A Remount. A Holy Grail touch holds the 20 EMA with its low above the 50-day. A Remount lost its 50 or 200-day for 5 or more straight closes.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the line. Five or more straight and it is a Remount.

wrong.A Holy Grail; the line was retaken: The Grail never loses the 50-day. Six closes under it is a Remount.
wrong.A 20 EMA pullback: This stock lost its 50-day, a far deeper break than a dip to the 20 EMA.

questions.story: The stock closed under its 50-day for six straight sessions. Then it closed back over it on volume.

questions.q: Which setup is it?
questions.why: A Slingshot. Its closes slip under the 4-day EMA of the highs for a few sessions. The buy is the close back over it. A Grail touches the 20-day EMA.
questions.lesson_line: Name the line that was lost. The 4-day line is the Slingshot; the 20-day is the Grail.

wrong.A Holy Grail: The Grail needs a touch of the 20-day EMA. This stock never got there.
wrong.A Remount: A Remount buys back a lost 50 or 200-day. This was a 4-day line.

questions.story: Closes slipped under the 4-day EMA of the highs for four sessions. The stock never touched its 20 EMA. Then it closed back over the 4-day line.

questions.q: What was the grade going in?
choices: A or B; 10 sessions, not A+
A+; all the boxes are ticked
Not a setup; it ran too long
questions.answer: A or B; 10 sessions, not A+
questions.why: An A or B. Our A+ is 2 to 5 sessions; 6 to 10 is an A or B. Ten days is a flag that has already lost its urgency, and the loss was a planned 1R.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days is a flag that has already lost its urgency.

wrong.A+; all the boxes are ticked: A+ is 2 to 5 sessions, shallow and orderly. Ten days is the far end of the range.
wrong.Not a setup; it ran too long: Ten sessions is still inside the 2 to 10 the card allows. It trades, graded down.

questions.story: A strong ADX push, then a 10-day pullback to the 20 EMA, the longest the rule allows. You bought at 84.24, stop 81.37. It stopped out with no excursion past 0.5R.

questions.q: Some web pages describe the Holy Grail with a 20-day simple average; Raschke names the exponential one.
questions.why: True. Woods writes a 20-period simple moving average; Raschke uses a 20-period exponential moving average. Our line is the 20-day EMA of closes.
questions.lesson_line: Follow the originator, not the rewrite. Exponential, every time.

questions.q: On the ADX session, what gives the trade its direction by our card?
choices: Price: the close above a rising 20 EMA
questions.answer: Price: the close above a rising 20 EMA
questions.why: Price. On the ADX session the close was above the 20 EMA, and the EMA is higher than 10 sessions earlier. +DI over -DI is not a gate.
questions.lesson_line: Strength from the ADX, direction from price. Keep the jobs separate.

wrong.+DI over -DI: A scanner's add-on, not Raschke's rule and not ours. Price decides direction.
wrong.The ADX itself: The ADX measures strength; a strong downtrend also has a high ADX.
wrong.The 50-day's slope: The 50-day is the floor under the touch. The 20 EMA and the close give direction.

questions.q: What comes off?
choices: A third at 5R, sell the burst
Nothing; let the whole leg run
All of it, sold at the 5R line
questions.answer: A third at 5R, sell the burst
questions.why: A third at 5R, then a big part into the climax run. After the first third at 3R: another third at 5R, then trail the last third. A climax run is sold into.
questions.lesson_line: Two trims by rule, then judgment: sell a big part into a vertical leg.

wrong.Nothing; let the whole leg run: Sell partials into strength. A vertical leg is the strength to sell into.
wrong.All of it, sold at the 5R line: 5R is the second third, not the exit. The last third rides the trail or the climax sale.
wrong.A third once it reaches 10R: The second third comes at 5R, not 10R. Waiting is giving it back.

questions.story: Bought at 91.78, stop 88.88. 3R in five sessions, a third off. Then the parabolic leg: three straight up days with gaps.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.why: 200. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. The touch session closes above it, or it is no trade.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day first. Then look at the line.
questions.sentence: No Holy Grail long below the ___-day simple moving average.

questions.q: Which is the one thing you never do?
choices: Tighten the stop to 3% to fit
Skip the trade and keep cash
Wait for a tighter trigger bar
questions.answer: Tighten the stop to 3% to fit
questions.why: Never raise the stop to fit. Stop first; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
questions.lesson_line: You never pick a size and back-fit a stop inside the noise.

wrong.Skip the trade and keep cash: Skipping is allowed. If the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip.
wrong.Wait for a tighter trigger bar: Waiting is fine. The mistake is moving the stop, not the entry.

questions.story: The swing low sits 5.5% under your fill. The honest stop breaks the about 3% habit.

questions.q: Which grades higher, and is volume a gate?
choices: The quiet one; a plus, not a gate
The loud one; buyers are back
Neither; both fail a volume gate
questions.answer: The quiet one; a plus, not a gate
questions.why: The quiet one grades up, and volume is not a gate. Our scan found a quiet pullback did not change much (27.6% against 26.7%), so it is a plus only.
questions.lesson_line: Light volume into the line is a nice touch. It is not the trade.

wrong.The loud one; buyers are back: Heavy volume on a pullback is selling, not buying. It grades down, a little.
wrong.Neither; both fail a volume gate: There is no volume gate. No source requires one.

questions.story: Two Holy Grails, same shape. One pulled back on half its usual volume, the other on 1.2x.

questions.q: A home-made ADX on a short window can read a trend where the true Wilder ADX reads chop.
questions.why: True. A plain-sum ADX read 29.9 on a chop chart where the Wilder ADX read 17.7. True ADX values take around 150 periods of data.
questions.lesson_line: Check which ADX you are reading before you trust the number.

questions.q: Take the trigger?
choices: Yes; a clean setup is the setup
Yes, at half the normal size
questions.why: No. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
questions.lesson_line: A clean touch in a thin stock is still a thin stock.

wrong.Yes; a clean setup is the setup: The setup is fine and the stock is not ours. The liquidity rule comes before the chart.
wrong.Yes, at half the normal size: Size does not make a thin stock liquid.

questions.story: A clean first touch of the 20 EMA on a $7 stock. It trades about $4 million a day.

questions.q: The highest close of the last 20 sessions printed 7 sessions ago; the touch is today. Does the test pass?
choices: No; it must be within 5 sessions
No; it must be a 52-week high
questions.why: Yes. The highest close of the last 20 sessions was made within the 10 sessions before the touch. Seven is inside ten.
questions.lesson_line: Count back from the touch. Ten sessions is the window for the high.

wrong.No; it must be within 5 sessions: The window is 10 sessions, not 5. The A+ length is a different row.
wrong.No; it must be a 52-week high: A 20-session closing high is the test. A 52-week high is not required.

questions.q: By our rules, what came off on the way up?
choices: A third at 3R and a third at 5R
questions.answer: A third at 3R and a third at 5R
questions.why: Two thirds banked. A third at 3R, a third at 5R, stop at breakeven, the last third on the 10-day trail. CI reached 3R in 2 sessions and ran to 12.9R.
questions.lesson_line: Sell partials into strength. The trims are what you keep when the run ends.

wrong.Nothing; it had not reached 10R: Waiting for 10R with nothing banked is how a winner becomes a scratch.
wrong.All of it at 5R: The last third rides the trail. 5R is the second trim, not the exit.

questions.story: Bought at 36.72, stop 36.03, the morning after a first touch. It reaches 3R in two sessions and keeps going for weeks.

questions.q: How many do you take on day one?
choices: A few, then add as they work
All seven; Green means full risk
None; wait a week to be sure
questions.answer: A few, then add as they work
questions.why: A few. After a correction, when the reading turns Green again, start with a few positions and add as they work.
questions.lesson_line: Green after a correction: a few positions first. Let the winners earn the next ones.

wrong.All seven; Green means full risk: Full risk per grade is the ceiling, not the first day's order. Earn it.
wrong.None; wait a week to be sure: Waiting a week after the turn is how you miss the first leg. A few is the rule.

questions.story: After a correction the reading just turned Green. Your list shows seven leaders at their first touch of the 20 EMA after a strong push.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
choices: Limit order; ATR stop; out at 2R
Buy the touch; line stop; hold
questions.why: A market order as it trades over the prior day's high. The stop sits a few cents under the swing low, and a third comes off at 3R. EXPD got to 3R in three sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open; execute it without a debate.

wrong.Limit order; ATR stop; out at 2R: Entries are market orders, and a stop a full ATR under the low is the named mistake. Out at 2R skips the 3R trim.
wrong.Buy the touch; line stop; hold: Buying the touch is the named mistake, and a stop at the line sits inside the pullback.

questions.story: EXPD, March 2006: a three-day, 3.6% rest to the 20 EMA after a fresh momentum high. This morning it trades over the prior day's high.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the touch day. A first pullback to the rising 20 EMA after a strong push. Take the trigger or pass?
choices: Take it; the low holds the 50-day
questions.answer: Take it; the low holds the 50-day
questions.why: Take it. The first touch since the push, the low holding over the 50-day, the close above the 200-day. A strong October thrust, seven quiet red days into the line; it triggered the next morning and never looked back.
questions.lesson_line: Young trend, first touch, floor intact: that is the context. Then wait for the trigger.

wrong.Pass; the touch broke the 50-day: Look again: the low sits well above the 50-day here.
wrong.Pass; price is under the 200-day: Price sits well above the 200-day, resting on its 20 EMA.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the day it touches the 20 EMA and holds. Is the touch above the 200-day? Take it or pass.
choices: Pass; it is under the 200-day SMA
Take it; the 20 EMA held the touch
Take it; the ADX is strong
questions.answer: Pass; it is under the 200-day SMA
questions.why: Pass. The touch closed at 51.44 under the 200-day at 52.79. The trade that followed ran to 5.4R and the rule still says no; location is a rule, not a prediction.
questions.lesson_line: A setup that works is not always our setup. The 200-day decides before the line does.

wrong.Take it; the 20 EMA held the touch: The line held and the location failed. No longs under the 200-day.
wrong.Take it; the ADX is strong: A sharp rally can push the ADX up under the 200-day. The location rule still says no.

questions.q: Your Holy Grail long is up 2R and earnings are tomorrow. You hold through the report.
questions.why: False. We hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R. At 2R it is not.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings is a gap you cannot stop. Five R buys the ticket; 2R does not.

questions.q: Which setup is it?
choices: A U&R at a swing low
questions.why: An Oops. It opens under the prior close, trades under the prior day's low and reclaims the prior close the same day. A Grail's trigger comes after a touch of the 20 EMA.
questions.lesson_line: Read the trigger. One day's open-and-reclaim is the Oops; a touch and a push over the high is the Grail.

wrong.A Holy Grail pullback: It never touched its 20 EMA, so there is no Grail. The Grail is bought after a touch of the line.
wrong.A U&R at a swing low: A U&R dips under a bigger prior low, a swing low, and can take up to 3 sessions to reclaim it. This was one candle under yesterday's low.

questions.story: The stock opens under yesterday's close and trades under yesterday's low. By the bell it has reclaimed yesterday's close. It never touched its 20 EMA.

questions.q: A one-session dip to the 20 EMA that bounces the next day counts as a Holy Grail pullback.
questions.why: False. Length is 2 to 10 sessions from the momentum high to the touch. Raschke's first retracement was two to three days; one day is a wobble, not a rest.
questions.lesson_line: A rest has to last long enough to shake someone out. One day does not.

questions.q: By our card, where does the buy stop sit for Wednesday?
choices: Cancel it; a lower low ends the setup
questions.why: Just over 52.00. Raschke puts the buy stop above the previous bar's high, and our card rolls it down while the setup is alive.
questions.lesson_line: The buy stop follows the latest high down.

wrong.Still over 52.40, Monday's high: Monday's level is stale. The buy stop follows the latest bar's high while the setup is alive.
wrong.Cancel it; a lower low ends the setup: A lower low does not end it. A close under the 50-day does, or 5 sessions from the first touch with no trigger.

questions.story: Monday touched the 20 EMA. Your buy stop for Tuesday sat over Monday's high of 52.40. Tuesday made a lower low and traded up to 52.00 without a trigger. The setup is still alive.

questions.q: By our card, after a lower low with no trigger, the buy stop stays over the touch day's high until it fills.
questions.why: False. The next trigger is that session's high, while the setup is still alive. The setup voids after 5 sessions from the first touch with no trigger.
questions.lesson_line: The trigger rolls to the latest session's high.
